brief.headline: Push for 8–10% price cut: they keep 8.5% profit vs peers' 4.8% — plenty of room

priceAsk.summary: Ask for 8–10% off current prices on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: ₹2.09 L to ₹2.62 L annual saving (8–10% of our ₹26.17 L spend)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 8.5% of sales as profit, almost double the 4.8% other packaging firms keep — there's room in their price. The open market for a 28 mm PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so asking 8–10% off is fair and defensible.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt, then offer to go to 15 days for another concession
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 30 days frees up ₹2.15 L cash for us; a further step to 15 days frees another ₹1.08 L

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni is healthy — no debt (0.00x), strong interest cover (75.84x), and sits in the safe zone (Altman Z 6.18). They keep 8.5% profit, well above the 4.8% peer median, so they can afford to give. But we're tiny to them — just 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue — so we have almost no pull on our own. Their cash is stuck for 124 days (vs 114 peer median), a bit longer than others, which means cash is slightly tight. Bundle this buy with other items, commit volume for a year, or name Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a credible second source to get their attention.

evidence.point: They keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% peer median — room to cut price
We are 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue — tiny customer, weak solo pull
Their cash is stuck for 124 days vs peer median 114 days — cash slightly tighter than others
Market ask for 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — supports our 8–10% target
evidence.figure: marketAsk.askBand: ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical: ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

evidence.point: Zero debt and 75.84x interest cover — financially strong, no distress
EPF payment delays flagged — minor compliance watch-out

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue; does pharma bottles, caps, preforms — top second-source candidate (health B 65/100)

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹946.50 Cr; pails, containers, pharma — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures (health B 73/100)

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (market backup)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India manufacturer; not yet priced or audited by us

risks: We're only 0.15% of their sales — on our own we have almost no weight; bundle volume or name a credible alternate to get traction
EPF payment delays on file — minor compliance flag; ask for assurance on labour payments before committing long-term
Their cash flow was negative ₹-6.59 Cr in FY2024-25 — they're healthy overall but watch that paying us faster doesn't squeeze them; tie early payment to a clear price benefit for us
Market backups (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Chemco, etc.) are leads only — qualify and price them before using in negotiation; don't assume availability or fit
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about price and payment — you're keeping 8.5% profit, well above the 4.8% your peers keep, and we think there's room for an 8–10% reduction, especially if we move to faster payment terms.
